newsitem.title: USA: Canada spot propane jumps, bidding wars on barrels.
newsitem.headline: Canada spot propane jumps, bidding wars on barrels.

text.p: Canada spot propane prices built continually this week, pressured higher by rising prices in the U.S. Midwest market and bidding wars over scarce barrels, traders said Thursday.
In Eastern Canada, spot propane hovered between 54.00 cents and 54.50 cents a gallon, 3.50 cents higher than last Thursday.
"This is a pretty firm market," said one Sarnia trader. "Inventories are just so low that there is a bidding war."
Supplies were also tight in Western Canada but much of the pressure on Edmonton spot material came from ballooning prices in the U.S. Midwest.
Edmonton spot propane jumped 4.00 cents to 46.00/46.50 cents in light trade.
"We're following the Conway market," said one trader, noting Conway barrels have traded 3.75 cents higher than Tuesday levels.
Activity in the other liquid gases was light, with normal butane prices remaining linked to the gasoline unleaded market due to the gasoline blending season.
Meanwhile, Gulf Canada Resources Ltd said Wednesday that a recent Alberta regulatory decision will allow it to double natural gas liquids output at its Strachan gas plant.
Under the agreement, Gulf would propane, butane and pentane-plus, but not ethane.
